THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND Revised 8/2016 Notice of Change form Notice of Change for: URI CON PMHNP Specialty Track in the MS Program and the Post-MS Certificate Program Date: October 7, 2021 A. PROGRAM INFORMATION 1. Name of institution University of Rhode Island 2. Name of department, division, school or college Department: Graduate Nursing College: College of Nursing 3. Intended initiation date of program change. Include anticipated date for granting first degrees or certificates, if appropriate. Initiation date: Sept 2022 First degree date: May 2024 4. Intended location of the program URI College of Nursing Graduate Program Nursing Education Center 350 Eddy St. Providence, RI 02903 5. Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages). The College of Nursing offers 3 nurse practitioner (NP) specialty tracks within its MS program and its Post-MS Certificate Program. These include Adult-Gerontology Primary Care NP, Family NP and Psychiatric-Mental Health NP (PMHNP). The first two of these specialties focus on primary care and are identical in terms of total credits in the MS Program (42) and very similar in terms of coursework and other program requirements. The PMHNP specialty track is the newest specialty track offered within the MS program

2 and currently requires 48 - 49 credits.
Having just graduated their first few graduates in the PMHNP specialty track, the PMHNP program faculty, the MS/DNP Program Committee and Associate Dean Kathy Hutchinson all agreed that revisions were needed within the PMHNP specialty track to address 3 issues.
The 3 issues and proposed changes to the PMHNP specialty track are outlined below and shown in Appendix A: (1) the credit allocations for some of the courses within the PMHNP specialty (e.g., NUR 545) needed to be corrected to be more consistent with university standards and other course offerings within the program.
NUR 545 focuses on psychiatric-mental health care for children, adolescents and families and is a 2 credit course.
In contrast, NUR 513 focuses on psychiatric-mental health care for adults and is a 3 credit course.

The didactic NP specialty courses in the other NP specialty tracks are all 3 credit courses. (2) In addition to correcting the inconsistency in credit allocations to didactic courses, the faculty and MS/DNP cmte. sought to address uneven distribution of clinical practicum credits across the PMHNP clinical courses (NUR 514, 546 and 547) and align these credits with those in the other NP specialty tracks.
The current PMHNP specialty requires 500- 600+ clinical hours and the 3 clinical courses total 15 credits.
In comparison, the other specialty tracks require similar clinical hours but allocate only 12 credits across their 3 clinical courses. (3) In order to be consistent with recommendations from our accrediting body (The American Association of Colleges of Nursing / CCNE), the CON implemented a single course addressing Advanced Health Assessment / Physical Assessment Across the Lifespan (NUR 530) In Fall, 2021.
This 4 credit didactic and lab course will now be completed by students in all 3 nurse practitioner specialty tracks in the MS program.
In the past, PMHNP students took an abbreviated 3 credit course in health assessment (NUR 501).

This change alone would result in an additional 1 credit increase to the PMHNP track of the MS curriculum.
The number of credits for this specialty track is already high.
Addressing the issues in (1) and (3) above would result in a 1 - 2 credit increase in the number of credits in the PMHNP specialty track.
Balancing this against the need to reduce clinical credits in (2) above, would result in an overall reduction in the number of credits for the PMHNP specialty track in the MS program from 48-49 to 47.
The individual course syllabi have been revised to reflect changes in pre-requisites (NUR 530 replaces NUR 501 as a pre-requisite for all the specialty courses [e.g., NUR 513, 514, 545, 546 and 547]).
The course descriptions have been clarified and the course objectives reviewed and edited slightly.
The descriptions for the clinical practicum courses (NUR 514, 546, 547) have been abbreviated and written more broadly to indicate that these courses focus on the application of previous and concurrent learning in a variety of practice settings.

3 These proposed changes to the PMHNP Specialty Track of the MS program result in minor changes to the PMHNP Specialty Track of the Post-MS Certificate Program, specifically a redistribution of credits across the PMHNP courses (NUR 502, 513, 514, 545, 546) as was described above. The total number of credits for the PMHNP Post-Master’s Certificate will remain at 20 credits. 6. Statutes, Regulations, and Policies Governing or Necessitating This Policy RIGL § 16-32 (“University of Rhode Island”) RIGL § 16-32-10 (“University of Rhode Island; Award of degrees – Curriculum and government”) URI Faculty Senate Constitution Article II―Powers University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Bylaws University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees Policy on Policies Reason for Policy/Purpose To ensure that the University’s policies are uniformly and consistently developed, approved, reviewed, and revised as needed in conformity with applicable statutes, regulations, and standards.

Forms Related to this Policy (Administrative) Policy Template (Administrative) Procedures Template Policy Statement A policy is a high-level statement of guiding principles and standards that articulates an institution’s values, communicates behavioral expectations, standards, and requirements related to a specific topic or area, or that otherwise provides guidance or rules for any component of an institution’s operations.
This policy pertains to the development and approval of policies at the University of Rhode Island (also, “University”) and, as such, provides guidance on both Academic and Administrative policies in order to provide transparency as well as coordination in the policy development process across the University.
Authority Approval of University policies will be: • In the case of Academic Policies, by the Faculty Senate and the President, consistent with RIGL 16-32-10 and Article II of the Constitution of the Faculty Senate, except where approval by the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees is required or appropriate.
In the case of Administrative Policies, by the Administrative Policy Committee, except where approval by the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees is required or appropriate.

Policy on Policies Effective: August 5, 2019 Page 3 of 5 DRAFT Development and Format Policy Owners are charged with overseeing the initial development , regular review, and timely revision of policies related to their area of responsibility.
Policy Owners shall be noted as positions, not named individuals. • Academic Policies shall be developed through processes outlined in the University Manual (see University Manual, Chapter 11).
A ll Academic Policies shall be in the form consistent with the general form of the University Manual, as controlled by the Faculty Senate. • Administrative Policies shall be developed by the particular units that manage the operational area of concern for that policy.
The form and content of Administrative Policies shall be consistent with the p olicy template developed by the Division of Administration and Finance. • All University Policies must be consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law and regulations.

Review and Approval All new and revised policies require approval. • New Academic Policies or material changes to existing Academic Policies require approval by the Faculty Senate and the President, and by the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees where approval by the Board is required or appropriate.
Once approved by the President, or the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees if required, the policy may be incorporated into the University Manual, with the information regarding this new policy or change disseminated to the University community and/or specific stakeholder groups, as appropriate. • New Administrative Policies or material changes to existing Administrative Policies require approval by the Administrative Policy Committee, and by the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees where approval by the Board is required or appropriate.
Prior to submission for such approval, draft p olicies must be reviewed by any office(s) directly responsible for implementing a substantive aspect of the policy.

Additionally, to the extent such policy or change in policy is not mandated in law or regulation, stakeholder groups likely to be materially affected by the proposed policy or change in policy sh all be given the opportunity to review and comment on the proposed policy or change to policy .
The development process for new or revised policies shall be managed by the Division of Administration and Finance, which shall maintain a working group responsible for stakeholder review and for recommending policies to the Administrative Policy Committee.
Once approved by the Administrative Policy Committee, or the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees if required, the new policy or change will be disseminated to the University community and/or specific stakeholder groups, as appropriate.

Training If training on a new policy or revisions to a policy is necessary or advisable, the Policy Owner (or proposing unit) will work with Human Resources Management (for staff), the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs (for faculty), and/or the Vice President of Student Affairs (for students), as applicable, to identify, develop, or otherwise make available appropriate training for the University community or relevant subgroup within the University community.

Policy on Policies Effective: August 5, 2019 Page 4 of 5 DRAFT Review/Revision Academic Policies shall be reviewed per procedures found in Chapter 11 of the University Manual.
Each Administrative Policy will state on its face a “Next Review Date” by which the policy will be reviewed by the Policy Owner and then by the Administrative Policy Committee should the policy revision include material changes.
Any University policy must be reviewed when there are changes in law, statute, or regulation, as well as changes to any University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees policy, that might affect the provisions of that policy.
Reviewed and revised policies shall be submitted through the same approval process as a new policy.
Repository and Archiving Academic Policies are instituted as elements of the body of the University Manual, with a notification within the University Manual (Appendix G) that Administrative Policies are found at the University’s Adminis trative Policies webpage (www.uri.edu/policies).
Administrative Policies are maintained at a central webpage as the single repository for these policies, with a notification that Academic Policies are found within the University Manual.

All previous versions of amended or revised Policies must be archived.
If a Policy Owner concludes that a policy within its oversight has no continuing applicability , the Policy Owner may propose retirement of the policy through the same review and approval channels set forth above for approval of policies.
Retired Academic Policies shall be incorporated into archived versions of the University Manual.
Retired Administrative Policies will be archived but accessible from the University Policy Website (www.uri.edu/policies).
Additional Information Nothing in this policy limits the authority of the University to issue, amend, or withdraw a policy.
Exceptions None

Center Review Subcommittee Report to the Faculty Senate Mar 16, 2022 Last year we processed changes to the University Manual (UM) that were voted on by this body.
We now are following up with an update to the section of the Bylaws where this committee's duties are described, as the duties no longer matched with the UM.
In reviewing the changes and in consultation with CBUM, it was noticed that a section of the UM was still vague and needed clarification.
Thus, with this report, we wish to present 1.
Changes to the UM for a vote and 2.
Changes to the Bylaws to be voted on at the next Faculty Senate meeting.
How to read this document: · The top three sections, 8.90.20, 8.90.30, and 4.44 are as they would read with the suggested changes. · The next three sections are markups from what is currently in the UM and Bylaws. o Strikeout is language being removed o Red is language being added that is mainly editorial o Blue is also language to be added, but not strictly editorial language.
The changes in the Bylaws section 4.44 is just a reflection of what is in the Manual sections 8.90.20 and 8.90.30.

1 FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE March 24, 2022 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2021-2022-7 At the March 3, 2022 meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate.
SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate PROGRAM CHANGES: COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Business Analytics and Intelligence major: In 2007, the Management Information Systems major was suspended due to low enrollment and resource constraints.
The refreshed major will be renamed Business Analytics and Intelligence and will be offered, along with the previously approved minor, to help prepare students to meet the high demand for professionals.
As companies are increasingly data-driven, there is demand for business professionals with knowledge, skills, and abilities in business analytics and artificial intelligence.
As a result, there are many job opportunities and high average starting salaries associated with positions at a wide range of organizations.

There was a strategic gift from Al Verrecchia to help develop student competencies in the Artificial Intelligence space, and the university previously reallocated resources required to offer the major again.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Accounting major: The program change makes the number of credits required in the Accounting major 120 instead of 121.
A four-credit course that was required as part of the major is no longer required.
Therefore, it is possible to complete the degree requirements with 120 credits.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: General Business Administration major: General Business will go back to being a separate major and will no longer be a track in Management.
The program change that was made last year (where students would start coursework in fall 2023) resulted in confusion for students, faculty, and stakeholders.
The General Business major previously served over 200 majors each year, which makes it a critical offering for the College of Business and the University.

Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Management major: The proposed program change streamlines the options in the management major and distinguishes the management major from general business.
General Business will go back to being a separate major and will no longer be a track in Management.
The program change that was made last year (where students would start coursework in fall 2023) resulted in confusion for students, faculty, and stakeholders.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Innovation and Entrepreneurship major: Update and revise requirements for major and minor as well as correct catalog copy.

The College of Business Administration offers a curriculum leading to the Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree with a major in management information systems (MIS)business analytics and intelligence (BAI).
The college also offers the Master of Business Administration (M.B.A.) degree with an opportunity for specialization in management information systems and the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree.
URI’s management information systemsbusiness analytics and intelligence major reflects the advanced technologies used in business and industry today.
Graduates earn a B.S. in business administration with an emphasis on computer applications, system analysis and design, and database managementstrategic applications of business analytics and artificial intelligence.
Graduates will possess skills in the application of microcomputer software and relatedbusiness analytics tools.
They will understand the value of “information” and the various technologies used to help organizations use information.

MIS BAI majors must receive a C or better in each prerequisite course for all management information systemsbusiness analytics and intelligence courses counting toward the major.
They must also receive a C or better in each MIS BAI course required for completion of the major.
Students will take the following courses for the major: BAI 356 (3), BAI 405 (3), BAI 455 (3), BAI 456 (3), BAI 457 (3) and three major electives from the following list: BAI 358, BAI 447, BAI 454, BAI 476, BAI 357, BAI 458, MKT 467, MGT 461 or other approved ACC, FIN, INE, MGT, MKT, SCA, or DSP course at the 300- or 400- level.
